items.followUp: Define transpiration and state one factor that increases its rate.

rubric.why: Identifies wind as moving air.
rubric.description: Defines wind as moving air.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that wind is air in motion.

rubric.why: Explains how wind affects water loss from leaves.
rubric.description: States that wind generally increases transpiration by removing moist air around leaves and maintaining a diffusion gradient.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that wind removes water vapour/moist air around leaves or otherwise increases transpiration.

modelAnswer: Wind is moving air.
Wind generally increases transpiration by removing water vapour around the leaves and maintaining a diffusion gradient for water vapour to leave the leaf.

items.followUp: Describe the structure of a vein and state one difference between a vein and an artery.

rubric.why: Describes the artery's strong wall.
rubric.description: States that an artery has a thick, muscular, elastic wall.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing the wall as thick and muscular or elastic.

rubric.why: Identifies a structural feature of the artery's passageway.
rubric.description: States that an artery has a narrow lumen.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the narrow lumen.

modelAnswer: An artery has a thick, muscular and elastic wall to withstand the high pressure of blood flowing through it.
Its lumen is narrow, and it carries blood away from the heart.

items.followUp: What is a heartbeat? Name the two phases of the cardiac cycle.

rubric.why: Identifies systole as the contraction phase.
rubric.description: Defines systole as contraction of the heart chambers.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for defining systole as contraction.

rubric.why: Identifies diastole as the relaxation phase.
rubric.description: Defines diastole as relaxation of the heart chambers.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for defining diastole as relaxation.

modelAnswer: Systole is the contraction of the heart chambers.
Diastole is the relaxation of the heart chambers.

items.followUp: Define an ecosystem and describe one interaction between organisms in a community.

rubric.why: Identifies that a population consists of members of one species.
rubric.description: Defines a population as organisms of the same species.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that a population consists of individuals of one species.

rubric.why: Includes the shared location that defines a population.
rubric.description: States that members of a population live in the same area.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for mentioning that they live in a particular or specific area.

rubric.why: Identifies the variety of populations in a community.
rubric.description: Defines a community as populations of different species living together.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that a community contains populations of different species.

rubric.why: Shows that the populations form a community by sharing a place and interacting.
rubric.description: States that these populations live in the same area or interact with one another.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for mentioning a shared habitat or interactions among the populations.

modelAnswer: A population is a group of organisms of the same species living in a particular area at the same time.
A community consists of populations of different species living together in the same area.
The organisms in a community interact with one another.

items.followUp: What are permanent tissues? Describe the function of xylem and phloem.

rubric.why: Identifies the defining feature of meristematic cells.
rubric.description: Defines meristematic tissues as tissues whose cells divide actively.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the cells actively divide.

rubric.why: Identifies apical meristem and its location or growth role.
rubric.description: Explains that apical meristem occurs at root and shoot tips and increases the length of the plant.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the name/location and 1 mark for explaining that it increases plant length.

rubric.why: Identifies lateral meristem and its location or growth role.
rubric.description: Explains that lateral meristem occurs along the sides of stems and roots and increases their thickness or girth.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the name/location and 1 mark for explaining that it increases thickness or girth.

modelAnswer: Meristematic tissues are made of actively dividing cells responsible for plant growth.
Apical meristem is found at the tips of roots and shoots; it increases the length of the plant.
Lateral meristem is found along the sides of stems and roots; it increases their thickness or girth.

rubric.why: States the catalytic role of enzymes.
rubric.description: Enzymes act as biological catalysts.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying enzymes as catalysts.

rubric.why: Identifies the usual chemical nature of enzymes.
rubric.description: Enzymes are proteins.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that enzymes are proteins.

rubric.why: States that enzymes act selectively on substrates.
rubric.description: Each enzyme is specific to a particular substrate or reaction.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for mentioning enzyme specificity.

rubric.why: Gives another characteristic of enzyme activity.
rubric.description: Enzyme activity is affected by temperature or pH, or enzymes remain unchanged and can be reused.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for any one of these valid characteristics.

modelAnswer: Enzymes are biological catalysts that speed up chemical reactions.
Most enzymes are proteins.
Each enzyme is specific to a particular substrate or reaction.
Enzyme activity is affected by temperature and pH; enzymes are not used up in the reactions they catalyse.

items.followUp: Explain how the large intestine absorbs water and how villi help absorption in the small intestine.

rubric.why: Describes bile's contribution to digestion in the small intestine.
rubric.description: States that bile emulsifies fats.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that bile breaks fat into small droplets or emulsifies it.

rubric.why: Explains how enzymes complete digestion.
rubric.description: States that pancreatic and intestinal enzymes complete the digestion of food in the small intestine.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming these enzymes or stating that they complete digestion there.

rubric.why: Identifies the adaptation that supports absorption.
rubric.description: States that villi increase the surface area for absorption.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for linking villi with increased absorptive surface area.

rubric.why: Describes where digested food is absorbed.
rubric.description: States that soluble nutrients enter blood capillaries and products of fat digestion enter the lymph.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing absorption into blood or lymph, with a relevant nutrient or fat-digestion product.

modelAnswer: Bile enters the small intestine and emulsifies fats into small droplets.
Pancreatic and intestinal enzymes complete the digestion of food into absorbable molecules.
The small intestine has many villi, which provide a large surface area for absorption.
Soluble nutrients pass through the villi into blood capillaries; fatty acids and glycerol enter the lymph vessels.

items.followUp: Define a tissue and give one example of an organ.

rubric.why: Defines an organ in terms of its component tissues.
rubric.description: Defines an organ as a structure made of different tissues working together.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that an organ consists of different tissues working together.

rubric.why: Provides a valid example of an organ.
rubric.description: Gives one example of an organ.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for any valid example, such as stomach, heart, leaf, kidney or lung.

modelAnswer: An organ is a structure made of different tissues working together to perform a specific function.
The stomach is an example of an organ.
